COVID19 - SA's PATIENT TESTING

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
COVID19 is here. With 61 and counting cases, the reality is we will not escape the virus. South Africans will die. There are measures in place. But are we ready and will these measures be taken seriou

Unique Selling Point:
NEWS

Summary:
President Ramaphosa gave a decisive and bold address on Sunday night. Non-essential travel – internationally and domestically is on hold. We are shutting our borders to foreigners. We are shutting our schools. Gatherings of more than 100 people has been prohibited.

These measures are great – but what’s happening on the ground?

We interviews infected patients, self-isolated travellers and get an inside scoop from an immigration insider working at OR Tambo Airport.

Further information:
TESTING
Some companies are insisting that employees do not come back to work if they have travelled to affected areas or are showing flu like symptoms unless they have been tested and have proof of a negative result. This sounds simple. But it’s not.

While private testing can be done at R1400 – it doesn’t mean you can just get tested. THERE ARE NOT ENOUGH TESTING KITS IN THE COUNTRY!!!!!! This is directly from Lancet Laboratories! People are going BOS! There was one man that got so angry when he was told he can’t be tested – he coughed on the Lancet technician, spat on his hand and wiped it in her face. The other challenge is that you may test negative today because the virus is still dormant, but you could test positive 3 days later.

I’m going to ask for an official Lancet interview – I think they will do it. If they don’t we have the insider.

I had a German case study who is meant to start work at Toyota – but he doesn’t want to be interviewed. This is not a crisis – we can still cover this through the LANCET Interview and in a link. We have more than enough for 10 min.

CASE STUDIES
1. ANDREW xx – COVID19 POSITIVE PATIENT, OLD MUTUAL DIRECTOR CAPE TOWN
Andrew travelled to London for business and stopped over in Switzerland to ski. He arrived back in SA last Monday. He had a sore throat, but he didn’t show a temperature when going through screening at the airport (I think in CPT). The man doing the screening had no mask and no gloves. Nor did the passport control immigration official. When he got home, he called his GP – Andrew wanted to get tested – he didn’t want to be responsible for infecting other people because he didn’t know he was infected. He started self-isolation at home and waited for the go ahead to do the test. It came two days later with an instruction to go to Chris Barnard – a public hospital. No one he came into contact with were wearing masks or gloves – no one seemed phased even when he told them he suspected he had corona. He was made to wait for 1.5 hours in a waiting room of about 20 people, some were pregnant women. When the medical staff eventually confirmed the test could be done – then they put on full hazmat kit! Did the test and told him to wait another half an hour – again with other patients. He was told to go home and wait for the results. By Thurday 10.00 Andrew got the results – his worst fears had been confirmed – he tested positive for Covid19. By Friday he had still not heard from Communicable Diseases.

His is outraged by how his case was handled. He is fearful of the spread of the virus. And said, while we think this is a first world disease, this will wiped out the third world. We are not ready.

THIS WILL BE A SKYPE INTERVIEW

2. DANE LOGIE – HIDDEN IDENTITY – SELF-ISOLATED NON-INFECTED TRAVELLER
Danie Logie was on the same flight as the KZN patient zero that travelled to Italy. KZN Health sent a medical official to his home within two hours of getting the call and had him tested. While his test was negative – he was advised to self-isolate for 14 days. He has done this. His test again came back negative and he has been cleared. While Dane’s case seems to have been handled better, he says he has been the subject of other people’s fear and paranoia. He has been treated as a leper by work colleagues and friends.

THIS WILL BE AN IN PERSON INTERVIEW – BUT HIDDEN IDENTITY

3. JEWISH SCHOOL PARENT - COVID19 POSITIVE PATIENT, JHB
I need to find this person still – will be good to compare how it’s been handled in Gauteng. I have details of the South African Board of Jewish Education.

THIS WILL BE A SKYPE INTERVIEW

IMMIGRATION SCREENING MEASURES AND SAFETY
I have a wonderful insider at OR Tamba – this woman will do a hidden identity interview. I will need to use an actor’s voice for her comments. She says:

Port Health screening is not top notch like they telling people and the media. Immigration Director only gave out masks like twice and then when they requested again for the next days he said it's finished. Gloves are not enough. Masks are not enough. Immigration officers got no sanitizer at there cubicles. She believes the virus will continue to spread because the most basic and crucial steps to prevent the spreading is not in place. Thousands of people could already be infected because of these inefficiency. She says she wants to speak because she doesn’t want blood on her hands.

EXPERT
We’re never going to get the Minister of Health or Communicable Diseases. But I think we could get someone from the World Health Organisation.

CALL OUTS
It would be great if we could widen out net and ask for people to take pictures coming through immigration at airports – My friend travelled back to the UK on Saturday and says some staff had masks, some didn’t, some had masks but had them around their necks. She sent me pics but they are out of focus – she was travelling with 3 and 5 years old and says they were awful ☺

Script:


STRUCTURE COVID19

VO: COVID19 is here, in South Africa – it’s in full swing and no one is immune. Confirmed cases increase every day.

President Ramaphosa first addressed the nation exactly one week ago.

UPSOUND RAMAPHOSA: Calls for an extradinory action… there can be no half measures.

VO: The President was decisive and bold. Non-essential travel – internationally and domestically is on hold. Our borders to foreigners are shut. Schools are closed. And gatherings of more than 100 people are now prohibited.

LINK: The threat of COVID19 spreading far and wide within South African borders is now a reality. Government measures to curb infection rates have been put in place since last week. But is it too late?

VO: It’s been 17 days since the first South African tested positive for COVID19. Currently, there are more than 200 confirmed cases in the country. The first local transmissions were recorded this week.
REREAD: ALTERNATIVE 300 graphic

DR GLASS: it's a completely new virus to humans, something we've never been exposed to before. M8

VO: Right now, there is no cure. The world is under lock down. With at least 90 countries closing its borders or instituting travel bans. The streets are empty in cities across the globe.

Virologist Dr. Allison Glass says the world’s never seen a virus on this scale in modern times.

MAC: Why is this is dfferent? (second question on reversals)
DR GLASS: We have had outbreaks in the past // but where they were quickly able to clamp down // because people were more ill so they didn't move around and were able to contain and bring transmissions to an end. // M35

VO: On Sunday, the 1st of March, South Africa’s Patient Zero, a 38-year old KZN man returned to Durban after traveling to Italy.

This man was on that same connecting flight from Dubai to Durban. He and his teenage son sat just three rows from Patient Zero. He has asked that we hide his identity for fear of victimization.

DANE: // The flight was full of sick people. There were people coughing all of us all around us. It was a cause of anxiety // INT2 M3

VO: Landing at King Shaka International Airport, there were officials in masks and gloves doing pre-cautionary screenings.

Four days later, he was contacted by the National Institute for Communicable Disease or NICD – they had been exposed to the virus. Worryingly, his son already had some symptoms.

DANE: He just had a cough and a snotty nose – so it was top of mind for me //pretty eager to get a test.. INT2 M7

VO: Within 20 minutes of getting the call from the NICD, a team arrived at his home.

DANE: // They put on fresh protective gear //There was the information about what they were trying to do. // They gave us temperature gauges. // They took swabs, throat and nose swabs, from both myself, and my son. INT4 MW

VO: Within 24 hours, the results confirmed they were both COVID19 negative. But to be safe, they still went into self-quarantine with daily calls from health officials.

But the hype around the virus was taxing, with both him and his son being ostracized professionally and in a school environment.

DANE: // It had got through my work and to clients, it had got through my son's school. And even though we had both tested negative and were in self quarantine and everything was sort of effectively fine - people panic// . INT4 M8

VO: In week two of the South Africa outbreak, there was an influx of potential infections around the country.

Andrew McPherson is under self-quarantine in Cape Town.

ANDREW: // I'm guilty of taking this too lightly I'm guilty of selfishly going on a ski trip and bringing this virus back to South Africa. // M21

VO: He tested positive for COVID19 when he returned to South Africa on the 9th of March after going to London for business, and then Switzerland for ski-ing.

Just getting the test done, proved a lot harder for Andrew in week two. It took two days for the NICD to refer him to a private hospital in Cape Town for testing.

ANDREW: they put me in a waiting room with other people. The nurse came and took my vitals and she didn't have gloves or a mask on - she was touching me// she was completely oblivious / M15/.

VO: COVID19 is spread through respiratory droplets that are released when an infected person coughs or sneezes, explains Dr Glass.

DR GLASS: If it settles onto a desktop…. and transferred though eyes, nose, and mouth that’s when it can transmit. INT1 M3 or M4

VO: Andrew believes COVID19 is already widely spread in South Africa. When he arrived a number of immigration officials at Cape Town International Airport were not wearing protective gear.

ANDREW: // You would cough on your hand your holding your passport// He takes my passport with bare hands. He scratches security stamps and gives it back to me. He then takes an experience possible. // That was a risk and there was no there were no barriers in place M6

VO: Protective gear at airports has been in limited supply according to this immigration official stationed at OR TAMBO International Airport, who spoke to us on condition of anonymity.

INSIDER: I don't want anybody's blood on my hands because OR Tambo, Department of Home Affairs, and the other stakeholders failed to take proper action. M20

VO: With the shortage of stock, immigration officials are expected to re-use gloves and masks.

INSIDER: // We are gatekeepers to a country and you are not taking precautions at that point. So what are we exposing ourselves to? // We have no sanitizer. // And we in the lion's den //

VO: This is not an ideal situation according to Dr Glass.

DR GLASS: // any contact between infected people and non-infected people is that is a risk. // that's just why it's so important that people who don't need it don't stockpile because it keeps it away from those who do need it. M25

VO: But the paranoia jumped from medical supply hoarding to grocery stockpiling, with South Africans buying up cleaning materials, toilet paper and basic foods.

LINK: So this is the situation in shops around SA – the shelves are empty – with people panicking with corona virus – my question is – is this really necessary.

ANDREW: // IF everyone in South Africa has got the resources that they need to protect themselves from the virus. We will sort this out. if it's only a few people have got the resources to protect themselves from this virus. It's going to decimate South Africa and it will impact on most people. M29

MAC: Are we equipped?
DR GLASS: // I don't think any country is equipped. To deal with it if it gets out of hand. // we're not going to be able to get rid of it immediately it's going to spread. Okay. But if we can slow that spread down so that we have. A smaller number of people requiring hospitalization we'll be able to cope /// M44

VO: Italy has surpassed China’s number of COVID19 deaths [3405+]. With daily new confirmed infections in the thousands [5000+], they’ve run out of hospital beds and are turning people away.

DR GLASS: this is real. It is a concern and I encourage people to watch on the news what's happening in places like Italy, places France the US // people // weren't taking this seriously they're still going to restaurants they were still socializing a lot. And that's just escalated the crisis. // M42

INSIDER: These are giant countries. These are superpowers, that are saying we cannot handle this. And here we have South Africa, a midget compared to those giants.

VO: As the world closes borders – travellers are forced to return to their home countries. 18 year-old Matthew Bracher was in Austria for a ski-instructor course when the virus was declared a pandemic.

MATTHEW: There is a possibility I was exposed while travelling to the airports. I have self quarantined myself just in case any symptoms do develop. INT1 M12

VO: Matthew arrived in Johannesburg in Week three - on Monday, the 16th of March – it appears things have improved at airports in terms of the prevention of transmission measures.

MATTHEW: When I arrived back in OR Tambo, maybe all the staff was wearing facemasks // INT1 M9
MAC: Were wearing gloves.
MATTHEW: Some of them are wearing gloves. Some of them not. I guess it just depends what they're dealing with. INT M20

VO: With the demand for tests increasing dramatically - both public and private laboratories are under strain.

LINK: As the fear of contagion spreads – there is a mad rush for testing. But there’s a global shortage of testing kits. The lab resources are limited. Just because you can afford to pay for test, doesn’t mean you’re going to get a test.

VO: The criteria for testing is simple – a person needs to have COVID19 symptoms and would have either been potentially exposed to the virus via high-risk travel or contact with an infected person.

DR GLASS: //there's no point in someone who's returning from overseas to test if they don't have symptoms. Because if you have a negative result it doesn't mean anything. You still going to have to do your two weeks of self isolation. So don't waste your time, don't waste your money if you're testing in the private sector. Don't waste the labs time and resources tasting unnecessarily. M26

VO: The health department warned that the demand for testing will spike in the coming weeks.

So far around 3% of the South African samples have tested positive. And while the infection rate is still climbing, patients are recovering - 80% of people will only have mild symptoms, as was the case with Andrew McPherson.

ANDREW: It’s such a mild sore throat .I mean I've gone to work I'm going to have plenty of times in my career. When I felt a lot worse than what I felt when I had this M9//

MAC: what will be the difference between an outbreak and survival. What needs to be done.
DR GLASS: Compliance and and a real sense of community. I think in China you know it was said this is what you will do and everybody listened. //South Africans are not very compliant //. M38// being a global community // it's so important that every country does their bit to get their own local outbreak under control so that they then don't become the new epicenter M13

VO: Flattening the curve of infection is crucial for South Africa, now more than ever.

ANDREW: Do not fear the virus, fear spreading the virus because that is what it is going to is going to destroy South Africa M27


PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: As South Africa continues to count the numbers and desperation to curb the outbreak mounts, we track down some COVID19 cases and ask if the country is ready for the impact?
PROMO 2
VO: An end to non-essential travel, a ban on gatherings of over a hundred people and schools shut down countrywide. But are these measures being taken seriously and can we stop the spread of COVID-19?

PROMO 3:
VO: COVID19 is here. With confirmed cases increasing every day, the reality is South Africans will be affected directly and indirectly. But are we ready and will emergency measures be taken seriously?

INT4 MW VO: Within 24 hours, the results confirmed they were both COVID19 negative. But to be safe, they still went into self-quarantine with daily calls from health officials. But the hype around the virus was taxing, with both him and his son being ostracized professionally and in a school environment. DANE: // It had got through my work and to clients, it had got through my son's school. And even though we had both tested negative and were in self quarantine and everything was sort of effectively fine - people panic// . INT4 M8 VO: In week two of the South Africa outbreak, there was an influx of potential infections around the country. Andrew McPherson is under self-quarantine in Cape Town. ANDREW: // I'm guilty of taking this too lightly I'm guilty of selfishly going on a ski trip and bringing this virus back to South Africa. // M21 VO: He tested positive for COVID19 when he returned to South Africa on the 9th of March after going to London for business, and then Switzerland for ski-ing. Just getting the test done, proved a lot harder for Andrew in week two. It took two days for the NICD to refer him to a private hospital in Cape Town for testing. ANDREW: they put me in a waiting room with other people. The nurse came and took my vitals and she didn't have gloves or a mask on - she was touching me// she was completely oblivious / M15/. VO: COVID19 is spread through respiratory droplets that are released when an infected person coughs or sneezes, explains Dr Glass. DR GLASS: If it settles onto a desktop…. and transferred though eyes, nose, and mouth that’s when it can transmit. INT1 M3 or M4 VO: Andrew believes COVID19 is already widely spread in South Africa. When he arrived a number of immigration officials at Cape Town International Airport were not wearing protective gear. ANDREW: // You would cough on your hand your holding your passport// He takes my passport with bare hands. He scratches security stamps and gives it back to me. He then takes an experience possible. // That was a risk and there was no there were no barriers in place M6 VO: Protective gear at airports has been in limited supply according to this immigration official stationed at OR TAMBO International Airport, who spoke to us on condition of anonymity. INSIDER: I don't want anybody's blood on my hands because OR Tambo, Department of Home Affairs, and the other stakeholders failed to take proper action. M20 VO: With the shortage of stock, immigration officials are expected to re-use gloves and masks. INSIDER: // We are gatekeepers to a country and you are not taking precautions at that point. So what are we exposing ourselves to? // We have no sanitizer. // And we in the lion's den // VO: This is not an ideal situation according to Dr Glass. DR GLASS: // any contact between infected people and non-infected people is that is a risk. // that's just why it's so important that people who don't need it don't stockpile because it keeps it away from those who do need it. M25 VO: But the paranoia jumped from medical supply hoarding to grocery stockpiling, with South Africans buying up cleaning materials, toilet paper and basic foods. LINK: So this is the situation in shops around SA – the shelves are empty – with people panicking with corona virus – my question is – is this really necessary. ANDREW: // IF everyone in South Africa has got the resources that they need to protect themselves from the virus. We will sort this out. if it's only a few people have got the resources to protect themselves from this virus. It's going to decimate South Africa and it will impact on most people. M29 MAC: Are we equipped? DR GLASS: // I don't think any country is equipped. To deal with it if it gets out of hand. // we're not going to be able to get rid of it immediately it's going to spread. Okay. But if we can slow that spread down so that we have. A smaller number of people requiring hospitalization we'll be able to cope /// M44 VO: Italy has surpassed China’s number of COVID19 deaths [3405+]. With daily new confirmed infections in the thousands [5000+], they’ve run out of hospital beds and are turning people away. DR GLASS: this is real. It is a concern and I encourage people to watch on the news what's happening in places like Italy, places France the US // people // weren't taking this seriously they're still going to restaurants they were still socializing a lot. And that's just escalated the crisis. // M42 INSIDER: These are giant countries. These are superpowers, that are saying we cannot handle this. And here we have South Africa, a midget compared to those giants. VO: As the world closes borders – travellers are forced to return to their home countries. 18 year-old Matthew Bracher was in Austria for a ski-instructor course when the virus was declared a pandemic. MATTHEW: There is a possibility I was exposed while travelling to the airports. I have self quarantined myself just in case any symptoms do develop. INT1 M12 VO: Matthew arrived in Johannesburg in Week three - on Monday, the 16th of March – it appears things have improved at airports in terms of the prevention of transmission measures. MATTHEW: When I arrived back in OR Tambo, maybe all the staff was wearing facemasks // INT1 M9 MAC: Were wearing gloves. MATTHEW: Some of them are wearing gloves. Some of them not. I guess it just depends what they're dealing with. INT M20 VO: With the demand for tests increasing dramatically - both public and private laboratories are under strain. LINK: As the fear of contagion spreads – there is a mad rush for testing. But there’s a global shortage of testing kits. The lab resources are limited. Just because you can afford to pay for test, doesn’t mean you’re going to get a test. VO: The criteria for testing is simple – a person needs to have COVID19 symptoms and would have either been potentially exposed to the virus via high-risk travel or contact with an infected person. DR GLASS: //there's no point in someone who's returning from overseas to test if they don't have symptoms. Because if you have a negative result it doesn't mean anything. You still going to have to do your two weeks of self isolation. So don't waste your time, don't waste your money if you're testing in the private sector. Don't waste the labs time and resources tasting unnecessarily. M26 VO: The health department warned that the demand for testing will spike in the coming weeks. So far around 3% of the South African samples have tested positive. And while the infection rate is still climbing, patients are recovering - 80% of people will only have mild symptoms, as was the case with Andrew McPherson. ANDREW: It’s such a mild sore throat .I mean I've gone to work I'm going to have plenty of times in my career. When I felt a lot worse than what I felt when I had this M9// MAC: what will be the difference between an outbreak and survival. What needs to be done. DR GLASS: Compliance and and a real sense of community. I think in China you know it was said this is what you will do and everybody listened. //South Africans are not very compliant //. M38// being a global community // it's so important that every country does their bit to get their own local outbreak under control so that they then don't become the new epicenter M13 VO: Flattening the curve of infection is crucial for South Africa, now more than ever. ANDREW: Do not fear the virus, fear spreading the virus because that is what it is going to is going to destroy South Africa M27 PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: As South Africa continues to count the numbers and desperation to curb the outbreak mounts, we track down some COVID19 cases and ask if the country is ready for the impact? PROMO 2 VO: An end to non-essential travel, a ban on gatherings of over a hundred people and schools shut down countrywide. But are these measures being taken seriously and can we stop the spread of COVID-19? PROMO 3: VO: COVID19 is here. With confirmed cases increasing every day, the reality is South Africans will be affected directly and indirectly. But are we ready and will emergency measures be taken seriously? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): COVID19 is here. With 61 and counting cases, the reality is we will not escape the virus. South Africans will die. There are measures in place. But are we ready and will these measures be taken seriou
metadata.Summary: President Ramaphosa gave a decisive and bold address on Sunday night. Non-essential travel – internationally and domestically is on hold. We are shutting our borders to foreigners. We are shutting our schools. Gatherings of more than 100 people has been prohibited. These measures are great – but what’s happening on the ground? We interviews infected patients, self-isolated travellers and get an inside scoop from an immigration insider working at OR Tambo Airport.
metadata.Further information: TESTING Some companies are insisting that employees do not come back to work if they have travelled to affected areas or are showing flu like symptoms unless they have been tested and have proof of a negative result. This sounds simple. But it’s not. While private testing can be done at R1400 – it doesn’t mean you can just get tested. THERE ARE NOT ENOUGH TESTING KITS IN THE COUNTRY!!!!!! This is directly from Lancet Laboratories! People are going BOS! There was one man that got so angry when he was told he can’t be tested – he coughed on the Lancet technician, spat on his hand and wiped it in her face. The other challenge is that you may test negative today because the virus is still dormant, but you could test positive 3 days later. I’m going to ask for an official Lancet interview – I think they will do it. If they don’t we have the insider. I had a German case study who is meant to start work at Toyota – but he doesn’t want to be interviewed. This is not a crisis – we can still cover this through the LANCET Interview and in a link. We have more than enough for 10 min. CASE STUDIES 1. ANDREW xx – COVID19 POSITIVE PATIENT, OLD MUTUAL DIRECTOR CAPE TOWN Andrew travelled to London for business and stopped over in Switzerland to ski. He arrived back in SA last Monday. He had a sore throat, but he didn’t show a temperature when going through screening at the airport (I think in CPT). The man doing the screening had no mask and no gloves. Nor did the passport control immigration official. When he got home, he called his GP – Andrew wanted to get tested – he didn’t want to be responsible for infecting other people because he didn’t know he was infected. He started self-isolation at home and waited for the go ahead to do the test. It came two days later with an instruction to go to Chris Barnard – a public hospital. No one he came into contact with were wearing masks or gloves – no one seemed phased even when he told them he suspected he had corona. He was made to wait for 1.5 hours in a waiting room of about 20 people, some were pregnant women. When the medical staff eventually confirmed the test could be done – then they put on full hazmat kit! Did the test and told him to wait another half an hour – again with other patients. He was told to go home and wait for the results. By Thurday 10.00 Andrew got the results – his worst fears had been confirmed – he tested positive for Covid19. By Friday he had still not heard from Communicable Diseases. His is outraged by how his case was handled. He is fearful of the spread of the virus. And said, while we think this is a first world disease, this will wiped out the third world. We are not ready. THIS WILL BE A SKYPE INTERVIEW 2. DANE LOGIE – HIDDEN IDENTITY – SELF-ISOLATED NON-INFECTED TRAVELLER Danie Logie was on the same flight as the KZN patient zero that travelled to Italy. KZN Health sent a medical official to his home within two hours of getting the call and had him tested. While his test was negative – he was advised to self-isolate for 14 days. He has done this. His test again came back negative and he has been cleared. While Dane’s case seems to have been handled better, he says he has been the subject of other people’s fear and paranoia. He has been treated as a leper by work colleagues and friends. THIS WILL BE AN IN PERSON INTERVIEW – BUT HIDDEN IDENTITY 3. JEWISH SCHOOL PARENT - COVID19 POSITIVE PATIENT, JHB I need to find this person still – will be good to compare how it’s been handled in Gauteng. I have details of the South African Board of Jewish Education. THIS WILL BE A SKYPE INTERVIEW IMMIGRATION SCREENING MEASURES AND SAFETY I have a wonderful insider at OR Tamba – this woman will do a hidden identity interview. I will need to use an actor’s voice for her comments. She says: Port Health screening is not top notch like they telling people and the media. Immigration Director only gave out masks like twice and then when they requested again for the next days he said it's finished. Gloves are not enough. Masks are not enough. Immigration officers got no sanitizer at there cubicles. She believes the virus will continue to spread because the most basic and crucial steps to prevent the spreading is not in place. Thousands of people could already be infected because of these inefficiency. She says she wants to speak because she doesn’t want blood on her hands. EXPERT We’re never going to get the Minister of Health or Communicable Diseases. But I think we could get someone from the World Health Organisation. CALL OUTS It would be great if we could widen out net and ask for people to take pictures coming through immigration at airports – My friend travelled back to the UK on Saturday and says some staff had masks, some didn’t, some had masks but had them around their necks. She sent me pics but they are out of focus – she was travelling with 3 and 5 years old and says they were awful ☺
